title: Croup and Noisy Breathing
hook: Croup's barky, seal-like cough can be alarming at 2 a.m., but most cases are mild and viral. Knowing how to calm your child — and the breathing signs that mean emergency — makes all the difference.
key_points: Croup is usually viral; it swells the voice box and windpipe, causing a barky, seal-like cough.
Stridor — a harsh, musical sound when breathing in — signals airway swelling.
Keep your child calm (crying worsens it); offer fluids; cool or humid air may ease symptoms.
Call 911/999 for real struggle to breathe, blue lips, drooling/can't swallow, or stridor at rest.
content_html: Croup has a sound parents never forget: a dry, barky cough like a seal, often worse at night. It's usually caused by a virus that swells the voice box (larynx) and windpipe (trachea), narrowing the airway. You may also hear stridor — a harsh, musical sound when your child breathes in — which signals that the airway is swollen. Most croup is mild and rides out at home over a few days.
extra_html: The single most useful thing you can do is keep your child calm, because crying and distress make the cough and the work of breathing worse — so stay calm yourself, hold them, and offer fluids. Many parents find cool night air or humid air soothing, though the American Academy of Pediatrics notes the evidence for steam is limited. The emergency signs are clear: a real struggle to breathe, bluish lips or fingernails, drooling or inability to swallow, or stridor while your child is at rest. Any of these means call 911 (or 999) or go to the emergency department right away. For milder croup that worries you, call your doctor. This is general guidance, not a substitute for medical care.

related.title: When to Call the Doctor — Red Flags
related.hook: Most childhood illnesses are mild, but a handful of signs mean don't wait and watch — get medical help right away. Knowing them takes the guesswork out of a scary moment.

related.title: The Common Cold in Children
related.hook: Young kids catch a lot of colds — that's normal. Colds are viral, so antibiotics won't help; comfort care does, and OTC cough-and-cold medicines aren't safe for little ones.

flashcards.prompt: What's the hallmark sign of croup?

choices.text: A rash that doesn't fade when pressed

flashcards.explanation_html: Croup is a viral swelling of the voice box and windpipe, producing its signature dry, barky cough that sounds like a seal.

flashcards.prompt: Why does keeping a child with croup calm matter?
flashcards.back_html: Crying and distress make the cough and breathing worse. Staying calm — and keeping your child calm — helps the airway settle. Cool or humid air may also ease it.

flashcards.prompt: Which sign means call 911/999 for a child with croup?

choices.text: Real struggle to breathe, blue lips, drooling/can't swallow, or stridor at rest
A barky cough that improves when the child calms down
A mild runny nose alongside the cough

flashcards.explanation_html: Visible struggle to breathe, bluish lips, drooling or inability to swallow, and stridor while at rest are emergencies — call 911/999 or go to the ER.
